title: post-tool-advisory's no-findings guard can never fire: critic always writes header lines to stdout, so a wired advisory hook prints on every Write/Edit
body:
**Found by dc 2026-08-25 while discharging an owed `critic` drive; verified independently by vc the same evening. The drive itself found NO defect -- `critic` is byte-identical through both binaries on a finding file and on a clean one -- and this is what the drive turned up on the way past.**

## The defect

`intent/plugins/claude/scripts/post-tool-advisory.sh:73` invokes `intent critic <lang>` and guards on `[ -z "$findings" ] && exit 0`. **That guard can never fire.** Both binaries always emit two `critic:` header lines, plus an `ok: no ... findings` line on a clean file, **all on stdout** -- which is the stream the hook captures.

Driven by vc on a deliberately clean file:

    rc=0, stderr EMPTY, stdout:
      critic: shell -- 2 of 6 rule(s) ASKED of this run; 2 armed in total. ...
      critic: shell -- 4 rule(s) could not be armed at all: ...
      ok: no shell findings at severity >= warning across 1 file(s)

So a wired advisory hook **emits an advisory on every single Write/Edit, findings or not.**

## Why that is a defect and not a preference

**The estate states the principle in its own words, three files away, in `session-finish.sh:46`: _a hook that fires identically every time carries no signal._** One principle, stated in one hook and broken in another.

## Not a port defect, which is what makes it a contract decision rather than a fix

**v2 does it identically.** It is INHERITED, so changing it is a `corrected`-class decision in the shape of `AC-07.3(a)`, not a WP-07 port fix. **dc routed it rather than editing a shipped hook to settle it, which is right.**

**Low urgency, deliberately: the hook is opt-in TWICE** -- it must be hand-wired into `settings.json` (it is not in the default stanza, ST0035 decision #4) AND `post_tool_use_advisory: true` must be set. Blast radius is small.

## THE CLASS, WHICH IS THE MIRROR OF THE ONE THAT PRODUCED IT AND IS THE REASON THIS IS WORTH FILING

`session-finish` (fixed at `a40cf763`) was **canon says the name exists and the door refuses it** -- a roster disagreeing with a roster. **This is the opposite: the door works perfectly and the CALLER'S guard clause can never fire.**

**NO ROSTER CHECK OF ANY KIND CAN SEE THIS ONE. No list disagrees with any other list; the rosters are in perfect agreement.** Finding it required running the command and reading **which STREAM the bytes came out of**.

**dc's statement of it, which is the durable output: A PARITY SUITE PROVES TWO BINARIES AGREE; IT CANNOT PROVE EITHER ONE IS USEFUL TO ITS CALLER.** If the hook surface gets further attention, that is the axis nothing currently covers -- and it is invisible to every instrument the estate currently has, because all of them compare an implementation to another implementation or to a declaration, and none of them asks whether the output serves the consumer that receives it.
